text:
Alex M.: Quick heads-up: the Go generator sample leaks goroutines when you cancel the parent ctx mid-stream. Minimal repro: start Generator(ctx...), read one token, cancel ctx; goroutine stays.

Priya D.: Which transport in the sample?

Alex M.: net/http. Looks like transport retry/auth refresh reopens stream and the prior reader goroutine never exits.

Omar H.: That's a known parity gap vs node/python where streams abort on cancel. We should add Close() to the iterator (io.Closer) that cancels the internal request context and ensures Next() returns context.Canceled.

Priya D.: Short term: update the sample app to `defer iter.Close()` and change the read loop to select on ctx.Done() too. Long term: make transport not auto-retry for streaming calls or add per-call flag `NoRetryOnStream`.

Alex M.: I pushed a tiny sample-app PR that uses `defer iter.Close()` and documents the cancel pattern. Will link.

Omar H.: I'll own the SDK change: add Close + unit tests that assert Next() returns quickly after Close(). Also add a CI leak check using runtime.NumGoroutine().

doc-bot: Created issue #2227: "go-sdk: generator stream cancel + retry race causing goroutine leaks" and added label bug.

Priya D.: Also add a Quickstart note so new users know to close streams or select on ctx.Done(). This comes up in onboarding a lot.

Alex M.: Thanks all; will follow up with PR link and test results.
